thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager - Routing anomalies detected for US cluster -> observed spillover to eu-west causing elevated latency and error rate. auto-mitigation suggested: disable spillover.

emma.ops: saw the pager, I'm on it. Can someone grab impact numbers?

maria-sre: looking now. initial telemetry shows 12% p50 latency increase for customers pinned to `tier:gold` and ~6% 5xx spike across the us region between 09:12-09:22 UTC.

sanjay-eng: confirmed. traces show a sudden shift of routed requests to `model-v2-quant` in eu-west due to fallback routing when us pool got saturated.

ingrid-product: any active rollouts to v2 today? customer impact?
maria-sre: no canary for v2 today, rollout was completed last week. Impact: a handful of high-SLA customers in US saw increased tail latency and some timeouts; CS flagged 3 customers so far.

emma.ops: oncall-bot, please handoff to current SRE oncall.

oncall-bot: Handoff to @maria-sre. Pager muted for others.

emma.ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable spillover flag globally, 2) pin gold-tier to routed US-only pool, 3) increase US pool capacity. Thoughts?

sanjay-eng: quick win is disable spillover. That's reversible and should stop eu-west routing while we diagnose. I can flip the policy in ~2m.

maria-sre: agree. Also want a log dump and routing decisions for that 10m window. Can you capture `routing_decisions` from the router service and `proxy-logs` from the ingress?

sanjay-eng: grabbing logs, posting snippets here. running: `rg "routeDecision" /var/log/router/*.log | sed -n '0912,0922p'`

--- logs ---
```
2026-03-11T09:12:07Z routeDecision: req=abcd1234 userTier=gold from=us-east -> route=us-pool fallback_enabled=true selected=eu-west model=model-v2-quant
2026-03-11T09:12:08Z routeDecision: req=abcd1235 userTier=silver from=us-east -> route=us-pool selected=us-v1
2026-03-11T09:13:02Z routeDecision: req=abcd9999 userTier=gold from=us-east -> route=eu-west selected=model-v2-quant (spillover triggered by capacity=true)
```

```
proxy: 504 from 10.4.2.12 -> 10.8.1.9 path=/generate latency=1204ms
proxy: 200 from 10.4.2.13 -> 10.8.1.5 path=/generate latency=110ms
```
--- end logs ---

maria-sre: that matches the hypothesis: spillover logic selected eu-west model-v2-quant for gold when US pool marked saturated. Need to know why US pool looked saturated. Could be continuous-batching backlog or a misreported metric.

emma.ops: sanjay, please flip `spillover_enabled=false` in the routing policy and confirm. Also add a temporary rule to pin `tier:gold` to `us-pool` so we have predictable behavior.

sanjay-eng: flipping now: `curl -XPOST https://config.redwood.internal/policies/route -d '{"spillover_enabled":false}'` -> 200 OK. Pinning tier: `PATCH /policies/route` with `pin_tier.gold=us-pool` -> 200.

emma.ops: any change in telemetry after the flip?

maria-sre: immediate drop in eu-west ingress for gold traffic. p50 back to baseline within 1-2 minutes. No new 504s in the subsequent 5m window.

ingrid-product: can we get a concise customer impact summary for CS and legal? They need who/what/when.

maria-sre: will compile. Short: 09:12-09:22 UTC, a subset of gold-tier US tenants experienced elevated latency/timeouts due to routing spillover to eu-west model variant. Root cause likely policy decision triggered by a transient saturation signal from the us-pool. Mitigation: disabled spillover and pinned gold-tier to us-pool at 09:15 UTC. Next steps: full RCA, add telemetry checks, evaluate fallback selection rules.

emma.ops: capturing timeline for RCA:
- 09:11:50 UTC - minor surge in us-pool queue length (batcher backlog).
- 09:12:07 UTC - router selects eu-west for first gold request (see logs).
- 09:12-09:18 UTC - spillover increases leading to eu-west saturation for some model variants, 504s reported.
- 09:15:32 UTC - mitigation: `spillover_enabled=false` and `pin_tier.gold=us-pool`.
- 09:17 UTC - traffic returns to expected routing.

sanjay-eng: hypothesis list to track in RCA: ["mis-tuned spillover threshold" , "batcher backlog misreporting" , "model variant compatibility causing backpressure" , "metric aggregation lag causing false saturation signal"]. I'll attach the router config snapshot.

--- router-config ---
```
spillover_threshold: 0.75
spillover_enabled: true
fallback_priority: [us-v1, us-v1-quant, model-v2-quant]
pin_tier: {}
```
--- end config ---

maria-sre: good. Also capture per-node GPU utilization and batch queue lengths for 09:10-09:20.

emma.ops: assigning action items: sanjay -> collect full router logs + config + heap traces (done partial here). maria -> compile customer impact and add to RCA doc. emma -> coordinate postmortem doc and timeline, schedule RCA sync.

ingrid-product: flag for product: evaluate whether fallback `model-v2-quant` should be in fallback_priority for gold tier at all. Might be causing cross-region cost/latency surprises.

sanjay-eng: note: there was a config push yesterday that lowered `spillover_threshold` from 0.85 -> 0.75 in an effort to reduce overload. I'll include the diff in the RCA.

maria-sre: thanks. We'll keep this thread as the single source of in-incident hypotheses and raw logs. Please paste any additional snippets here and tag me.

emma.ops: wrapping up live mitigation. Will create a private RCA doc with the timeline and findings. Scheduling a postmortem sync in 60m. Thanks all. :thumbsup
